rationale.conceptual: The model uses an established rate-theory framework (Brailsford-Bullough effective medium, master equations) but requires careful implementation of several interacting components: cluster size evolution, steady-state defect concentrations, sink strengths, and cascade production terms. Translating the paper's description into working code demands genuine understanding of radiation damage rate equations, placing it above a textbook operation but below a novel research-grade derivation.
rationale.execution: The pipeline is a simple 3-stage process: (1) run numerical simulation (save checkpoint), (2) export cluster distributions to CSV, (3) compute diffusion coefficients and write CSV. All steps rely on standard Python libraries (NumPy, SciPy) and straightforward file I/O. There is no complex orchestration, external tooling, or multi-source data assembly.
